gap_candidates.description: Add capability declarations for bridged providers to CLI_Bridged_Providers.md (matching language of direct providers): CAPABILITY_MULTI_ACCOUNT, CAPABILITY_SWITCH_NOTIFICATION, CAPABILITY_LANE_ATTRIBU… | Decision_Policy.md still lacks first-class concern/corroboration/promotion objects and their authority/lifecycle rules | Extend Decision_Policy.md with first-class policy objects and transitions for: concerns, corroboration, promotions, superseded/revoked/reopened states | Permissions_System.md permission snapshot invalidation on account switch must be defined explicitly | policy docs still assume a stronger single Puppet Master authority center
exact_missing_items: Add capability declarations for bridged providers to CLI_Bridged_Providers.md (matching language of direct providers): CAPABILITY_MULTI_ACCOUNT, CAPABILITY_SWITCH_NOTIFICATION, CAPABILITY_LANE_ATTRIBUTION, etc.
Bridge envelope must carry effective account identity and switch-reason when capabilities are declared
Permission reject-cascade and session-cache scope must be limited to actor/lane-aware boundaries, not whole session
Extend OpenCode SSE contract to filter events per actor/lane context
Decision_Policy.md still lacks first-class concern/corroboration/promotion objects and their authority/lifecycle rules
Permissions_System.md does not yet integrate the stricter requested/effective identity model that Contracts_V0.md now makes canonical
Architecture_Invariants.md needs to reflect newer runtime invariants like scheduler lane ordering and mutation-safe-point requirements
Extend Decision_Policy.md with first-class policy objects and transitions for: concerns, corroboration, promotions, superseded/revoked/reopened states
Require requested/effective identity fields in decision/permission records, not just runtime event records
Add architecture invariants for: canonical runtime object families, lane scheduler integrity, mutation-safe-point enforcement
Re-anchor blocked/HITL/policy flows on canonical node/attempt identifiers where appropriate
Define intent-specific orchestration/worktree modes explicitly, including single-branch exceptions and contract-unification conflict policy
Permissions_System.md permission snapshot invalidation on account switch must be defined explicitly

Rule: when effective_account_id changes for an actor/lane, all always/never approvals scoped to that (actor, tool, scope_context) where scope_context includes account-sensitive tools must be invalidated
Account-neutral tool approvals (e.g., read-only filesystem reads) may survive account switches if explicitly exempted in the approval scope definition
policy docs still assume a stronger single Puppet Master authority center
the rewrite now needs seam/package overseer scopes, blocked-owner attribution, and clearer separation between runtime/system/user authority
trust / permission decisions cluster: Permissions_System.md session cache and reject-cascade must be re-scoped to actor/lane-aware boundaries
Permission snapshot invalidation on account switch must be defined: when account changes, which cached permission decisions are stale
Always-approval and never-approval decisions must be scoped to (actor_kind, tool, scope_context) not to (session-global, tool)
Multi-actor permission snapshot isolation must be normative and testable
gap_candidates.blocking_reason: Concrete Plans/** document requires content reconciliation vs transfer obligation.
